gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-005 challenges the proof of the eigenfunction-convergence theorem and proposes compactness, whereas the gold issue concerns introductory prose overstating conditional subsequential spectral results as general spectrum convergence. The proof concern may affect the downstream claim, but it does not recognize the specific conditional-versus-general spectral statement.

The gold defect is failure of composition to descend from pointwise functions to L-infinity equivalence classes without null-set preservation. ISSUE-005 instead concerns projection convergence in an eigenfunction theorem; it provides no diagnosis of Koopman well-definedness or null-set behavior.

The gold issue is the ill-defined induced empirical operator caused by non-injective sampling and sampled-value quotienting. ISSUE-002 concerns FEM dimension-to-mesh scaling and cost exponents, with no recognition of empirical operator well-definedness.

Both entries identify the false clean covariance identity for noisy dictionary data, explain that the estimator concentrates around a noise-perturbed population operator, and recognize the resulting nonvanishing bias and need to revise the A_N error guarantee.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The asserted population covariance equals the clean Gram matrix despite additive dictionary noise; the omitted noise covariance shifts the limiting estimator and invalidates arbitrarily vanishing error around A_N.

component_coverage.gold_component: Additive dictionary noise changes E[gg†] and potentially the cross-covariance, so the empirical matrices do not target the clean matrices.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 explicitly supplies the noisy covariance identity, notes the resulting perturbed Bernstein target, and derives convergence to a biased operator rather than A_N.

component_coverage.gold_component: The noisy estimator cannot generally have arbitrarily small error around A_N as sample size grows without bias correction or additional noise information.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-003 states that the claimed error bound remains bounded below by asymptotic bias and proposes an explicit bias term, preserving only the sampling-error part.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns converting a conditional bound on the intersection of M truncation events, whose probability is p̃_N^M, into an unconditional confidence statement. ISSUE-003 concerns covariance-induced estimator bias and does not recognize the joint-event probability or confidence calibration error.

Both entries identify the invalid use of a fixed-vector projection convergence assumption on the varying sequence A f_N, and both connect that unsupported residual-vanishing step to the eigenfunction-limit argument. ISSUE-005 gives compactness as a sufficient repair, while the gold also notes the weaker pairing argument.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The projection assumption only gives convergence for each fixed test vector and cannot by itself establish norm convergence of (I-P_{F_N})A f_N when f_N varies with N; using it that way leaves the residual step unsupported.

component_coverage.gold_component: The fixed-vector projection assumption does not imply norm convergence of the residual applied to the varying sequence A f_N.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-005 explicitly states that the assumption is applied to the varying vector A f_N rather than a fixed test vector and explains why the claimed residual limit is unsupported.

component_coverage.gold_component: This unsupported residual step is used in identifying weak limits as eigenfunctions; a valid argument must instead use the appropriate fixed-test-vector pairing or add a sufficient hypothesis.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-005 connects the failed residual limit to the unproved eigenfunction theorem and gives compactness as a condition that supplies the missing strong convergence.
